stories.headline: Watch Ritchie Blackmore return to the stage with Deep Purple - Louder
stories.summary: The ice has thawed: Ritchie Blackmore has performed with Deep Purple for the first time in 33 years
stories.why: Ritchie Blackmore is the architect of heavy metal guitar—his neoclassical style defined Deep Purple and influenced everyone from Yngwie to modern metal. A 33-year reunion signals that even the most fractious creative partnerships can heal, reshaping how you think about unfinished business in your own life.

stories.headline: Roseanne Barr’s son claims sitcom’s cast conspired to take her show from her during social media controversy - Page Six
stories.summary: The “Roseanne” reboot was cancelled in 2018 over its title character’s polarizing tweet.
stories.why: This is the dark side of cancel culture you actually lived through: a working-class icon lost her empire over one tweet, and now her family is publicly litigating whether the industry coordinated her takedown. It's a litmus test for whether consequences are proportional or weaponized.

stories.headline: 'DWTS' Gleb Savchenko Calls Ex's Claim Authorities Are Searching for Him a 'Total Lie' - TMZ
stories.summary: Gleb Savchenko is firing back at his ex-wife's claim authorities are trying to track him down with their teenage daughter ... calling the allegation a "total lie" in a new court filing.
stories.why: A Dancing with the Stars pro's custody battle playing out in tabloids shows how reality TV fame creates real liability—his reputation hangs on court filings, not performances. It's a cautionary tale about the cost of chasing celebrity relevance.

stories.headline: ‘The Traitors: New Blood’ Season 1 Cast: Meet the 22 Civilian Contestants - The Hollywood Reporter
stories.summary: The NBC reality competition series, hosted by Alan Cumming, premieres Sept. 17.
stories.why: This is the format that broke streaming and rewired reality TV competition; it's designed for your exact age group's taste for psychological gamesmanship over athletic spectacle. If you haven't experienced it yet, this is the cultural moment to understand why your friends are obsessed.

stories.headline: ‘End of Oak Street’ Box Office Aims to Take Bite Out of ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ - The Hollywood Reporter
stories.summary: 'PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie' is among the new offerings for the weekend as Tom Holland's web-slinger looks to continue a historic run.
stories.why: Tom Holland's Spider-Man is on a historic box office run that's reshaping franchise economics; this is a masterclass in IP dominance and why studios bet everything on sequels. The fact that other films are literally named around competing for scraps shows the current Hollywood hierarchy.

stories.headline: DGA and IATSE Push Rob Bonta to Allow Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger With Conditions - Variety
stories.summary: The Directors Guild of America and IATSE urged California Attorney General Rob Bonta to settle its antitrust case with Paramount.
stories.why: A Paramount-Warner Bros. merger would reshape which movies get made and distributed for the next decade; guilds are fighting because consolidation historically means fewer jobs and lower residuals. This directly affects whether mid-budget films—the ones you actually want to watch—still get greenlit.

stories.headline: StubHub Is Spending Millions Trying to Stop a Bill That Would Cap Concert Ticket Resale Prices - The Hollywood Reporter
stories.summary: It's shelling out more money than Chevron, Verizon, AT&T and OpenAI this quarter to beat California legislation that would limit mark ups to no more than 10 percent more than the original price tag.
stories.why: StubHub is spending more on lobbying than tech giants to preserve concert markup inflation; this is the moment you realize the resale market actively *opposes* affordable live music. It crystallizes why tickets to see your favorite band cost $200 before fees.
